The minimum distance of the dual line‑point code in higher‑dimensional projective space grows by the size of a projective \((n-2)\)-subspace.  Precisely, for every \(n>2\)

\[
\boxed{ \displaystyle d(n,q)=\Bigl(\sum_{i=0}^{\,n-2} q^{\,i}\Bigr)\; d(2,q)
      \;=\; \frac{q^{\,n-1}-1}{q-1}\; d(2,q)\,. }
\]

This expresses \(d(n,q)\) solely in terms of the plane value \(d(2,q)\), the field size \(q\), and the dimension \(n\).  

**ANSWER:** \(d(n,q)=\bigl(\sum_{i=0}^{n-2} q^{i}\bigr)\,d(2,q)=\dfrac{q^{\,n-1}-1}{q-1}\,d(2,q)\).
